thesisQuality.note: Approximately 40,000 U.S. towers and independent 23% year-over-year mobile traffic growth support durable demand, offset by company-specific churn.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: More than $7B debt reduction improved resilience while 2026 site-rental guidance remains churn-pressured.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: Sep. 30 market data show $66.65 close, $28.36B market cap, $50.72B EV, 16.82x price/FFO and 6.38% yield; valuation reset offers headroom but leverage and growth uncertainty remain.

catalystScore.note: Post-divestiture cost/debt actions and the next operating update can clarify normalized tower growth, but catalyst realization remains execution-dependent.

governancePower.note: Management executed the divestiture, debt reduction and $1B repurchases, while post-sale growth durability remains unproven.

alignment2036.note: Macro towers support durable connectivity needs and independent data show strong North American traffic/5G adoption, though carrier spend can shift architectures.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: The divestiture created a pure-play U.S. tower company, reducing independent demand engines and increasing dependence on one infrastructure class and carrier set.

bottleneckControl.note: Permitted, sited macro towers provide meaningful physical scarcity and colocation utility, but carriers retain alternative spend paths.

scenarioRobustness.note: Long contracts and fixed-rate debt improve resilience, but about 93% of first-half site-rental revenue came from three carriers.

substitutionResilience.note: Macro sites remain important for coverage/capacity, but incremental spend can shift toward small cells, fiber, spectrum efficiency or satellite.

supplyChainResilience.note: Domestic long-lived physical assets and repaired financing reduce conventional supply exposure, while geographic and carrier-deployment dependence remain.

pricingPower.note: About five years weighted-average contract term and $22.1B expected future cash inflows support visibility, but concentration and cancellation/default risk constrain pricing power.

risk.note: Three-carrier concentration, tenant cancellation/default exposure, reduced diversification and alternative architectures remain material risks.

confidence.note: Recent issuer, SEC, independent industry and current market evidence provide broad coverage; normalized post-DISH leasing growth remains unresolved.

thesis: Crown Castle is a strategically relevant U.S. macro-tower pure play with scarce physical sites, long contracts and repaired financing, but carrier concentration and churn limit robustness.
keyRisk: Carrier consolidation, cancellations or capital reallocation away from macro towers can impair leasing growth.
nextCatalyst: Third-quarter 2026 results and updated tower organic-growth/AFFO outlook.
